seed_commits.message:
chore: initial warehouse scaffold

DuckDB rather than Spark. The whole warehouse is one file, so the pipeline is
reproducible on a laptop with no cluster, no JVM and no credentials -- which is
what lets the tests assert exact totals instead of ranges.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(db): define the medallion schema in one place

Every CREATE is IF NOT EXISTS and the whole script is applied on connect, because an
ETL job is restarted far more often than it is first run. Money is BIGINT cents and
timestamps are UTC instants; both choices are load-bearing and documented where they
are declared.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(bronze): load the landing zone at most once

The load log is keyed on (source_file, content_hash) and written in the same
transaction as the rows. Keying on the filename alone would skip a corrected
re-export; keying on mtime would reload a byte-identical re-delivery. A line that
is not valid JSON is kept rather than dropped -- bronze is the only layer that will
ever know it arrived.
seed_commits.author: Tomás Oliveira <tomas.oliveira@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(silver): parse, normalise to UTC, dedupe, quarantine

A naive timestamp is rejected rather than assumed to be UTC: assuming shifts an event
across a day boundary for every customer in a negative offset and nothing downstream
can detect it. A decimal in amount_cents is rejected rather than rounded. Dedupe
orders by ingested_at then source_file then rowid, so two rebuilds of the same bronze
agree even when two files land in the same second.
seed_commits.author: Tomás Oliveira <tomas.oliveira@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(gold): roll up against a collapsed account dimension

bronze_accounts holds one row per delivery, so joining it raw multiplies every event
for an account that appeared in two exports. That inflates revenue, raises nothing,
and is caught only by the reconciliation. The join is against a row_number() view and
is a LEFT JOIN, so usage for a missing dimension row is counted with a NULL plan
rather than lost.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(watermark): forward-only, and only over work that finished

advance_watermark raises on a backwards move instead of clamping, and the context
manager runs the work before advancing. Advancing first means an exception leaves the
watermark past data nobody processed, and that window is never looked at again.
Position comes from event time, not the clock: usage telemetry arrives late as a
matter of course.
seed_commits.author: Ingrid Halvorsen <ingrid.halvorsen@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(quality): six gates, reported together

Each check returns a finding rather than raising, so one run tells the on-call
engineer everything that is wrong. The reconciliation leads: every other gate could
pass while the rollup quietly double-counted a join.
seed_commits.author: Ingrid Halvorsen <ingrid.halvorsen@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(pipeline): run the layers in order and gate the watermark

Quality gates run before the watermark moves, because the watermark records what has
been successfully processed. strict=False changes whether a failing gate raises, never
whether the watermark advances.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(profile): describe a delivery before ingesting it

A schema change upstream, a truncated export or a shifted null spelling are all cheap
to see here and expensive to find three layers later. Profiling never rejects anything;
rejection belongs to silver, with a reason attached.
seed_commits.author: Tomás Oliveira <tomas.oliveira@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(cli): etlduck run, bronze, silver, gold, check, profile, watermark

Every subcommand exits non-zero when the thing it did failed, because the scheduler
only looks at the exit code.
seed_commits.author: Ingrid Halvorsen <ingrid.halvorsen@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
feat(compat): a four-method Spark-shaped facade over DuckDB

So the notebooks read like Spark and run without a JVM. Deliberately minuscule:
anything more becomes a half-reimplementation of a distributed engine, which is a far
worse thing to own than some SQL. The docstring is explicit that there is no cluster.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: add the seeded landing-zone generator

Fixed seed, so it emits the same bytes on every platform and the suite can assert
exact totals. The defects are deliberate and fixed: per day one unparseable line, one
naive timestamp, one unknown event type, one decimal amount and one event with no
account, plus a replayed event across days. A generator that only produced clean rows
would let every one of those bugs through.
seed_commits.author: Tomás Oliveira <tomas.oliveira@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
test: cover idempotency, parsing, rollups, watermarks and the gates

Numeric expectations are hand-computed with the arithmetic in the docstring. Every
quality gate is tested in both directions -- a gate that has only ever been seen to
pass is not known to work.
seed_commits.author: Ingrid Halvorsen <ingrid.halvorsen@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
perf: add a pipeline benchmark

Reports the SQL statements issued per input row rather than only timings. Wall clock
under Docker varies severalfold; statements per row does not, and it is the figure
that reveals a per-row insert turning quadratic. Generates volume into a scratch
directory, never into raw/.
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
chore(dbx): add the Databricks-shaped job, policy and notebook assets

Shaped like the platform team's real assets so the same person can read both. Nothing
here submits to a cluster -- spark_compat.py says so at length -- but the constraints
the policy encodes are the ones this pipeline is written to respect, starting with
session timeZone pinned to UTC.
seed_commits.author: Tomás Oliveira <tomas.oliveira@example.com>

seed_commits.message:
ci: run the suite, parse the dbx assets, prove the pipeline is idempotent

ci/run_ci.sh mirrors the workflow so the same steps run locally. The pipeline smoke
test is its own file so both call it rather than each carrying a copy -- two inline
copies of a check are two things to keep in step, and the one that drifts is always
the one nobody runs locally.
seed_commits.author: Ingrid Halvorsen <ingrid.halvorsen@example.com>

seed_commits.message: docs: document the layer contracts, idempotency and the numeric choices
seed_commits.author: Priya Raghavan <priya.raghavan@example.com>

setup_commands: make test   # expect failures: reproducing them is step one
make run    # the pipeline end to end, then the quality gates
